newsitem.title: JAPAN: DKB declines comment on report of 'sokaiya' loans.
newsitem.headline: DKB declines comment on report of 'sokaiya' loans.

text.p: Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd (DKB) on Tuesday declined to comment on a newspaper report that it had made loans of three billion yen in 1990 to a company linked to a "sokaiya" racketeer.
"We do not comment on our deals," said a bank spokesman.
The daily Yomiuri Shimbun reported on Sunday that the company that received the DKB loans was also suspected of receiving stock trading profits transferred illegally from Nomura Securities Co Ltd.
The paper said the Dai-Ichi Kangyo loans, which were in addition to 3.1 billion yen in loans extended to the firm in 1989, were made without meaningful collateral and could become irrecoverable.
The 1990 loans were made through DKB and its affiliated nonbank money lender, the paper said.
The paper said prosecutors, currently investigating the Nomura incident, which came to light in March, were looking at the 1990 DKB loan for a possible link between the racketeer and the bank.
A spokesman for the Tokyo prosecutor's office declined to comment on the investigation.
